prompt: Asked the AI to check the whole project - not just recent changes - against the rubric, including whether tests, design docs, and AI logs were actually complete.
ai_output: Ran the frontend test suite live and confirmed all 18 tests passed. Disclosed that the backend test suite could not be run in the AI's own sandbox due to a network restriction, and asked for it to be run and confirmed independently instead of assuming it would pass. Checked git commit history and pointed out that only 2 large commits existed, which is thin evidence against the rubric's "regular commits" criterion. Searched the entire repository and confirmed no AI log or reflection file existed yet from anyone on the team.
decision: accepted the assessment as accurate; had the backend tests run and confirmed manually afterward (15/15 passed)
notes: The AI was explicit about what it could and couldn't verify itself, rather than claiming untested code definitely worked.

prompt: Uploaded the team's formal Assignment Submission Guide (required folder structure) and asked whether the project aligned with it.
ai_output: Cross-checked every required file/folder in the guide against the real repository. Confirmed the Inspections module's own required files existed. Separately identified group-level gaps not owned by any one student (problem-statement.md and architecture.md still empty, deployment.md unfilled, two teammates' folders still TODO). Flagged that the guide specifically requires .jsonl files exported from Claude Code, while this project had used the Claude chat interface throughout - explicitly recommended asking the tutor rather than assuming either interpretation was safe.
decision: escalated the AI-log format question to the tutor instead of accepting the AI's own guess
notes: Chose not to let the AI unilaterally resolve an ambiguity that a human authority should decide.

prompt: Asked the AI to check whether the Inspections module still worked correctly after teammates had merged a large amount of new work (real authentication, a restructured "Lift Workflow" UI, a new standalone Defects module, real Cloudinary uploads elsewhere in the app).
ai_output: Pulled the live repository from GitHub directly and diffed every Inspections-related file against the original merge. Found the backend controller had been safely extended by a teammate (soft-delete, schedule-consistency checks, Staff-role restrictions); found the original tests would now fail since they never authenticated as any user; found defect photos still used an old base64 approach while the rest of the app had moved to real Cloudinary uploads.
decision: asked follow-up questions about how the new standalone Defect model related to the existing embedded defects array before agreeing anything needed to change
notes: Did not accept the AI's summary as sufficient justification on its own - asked to see the actual model code and diffs first.

prompt: Approved migrating DefectEditor to the real upload system and rewriting the stale design docs, and asked for the changes to be packaged for review rather than applied silently.
ai_output: Migrated the photo-upload logic to the app's existing shared upload hook, matching a sibling feature's pattern rather than inventing a new one. Rewrote the database schema and API documentation to describe the auth rules, soft-delete/cascade behaviour, and schedule-consistency checks added by teammates. Packaged the change set with instructions rather than assuming direct write access to the repository.
decision: accepted only after personally reviewing the full git diff before committing
notes: Consistently reviewed the actual diff output before every commit throughout the project, not just at this point - treated as a non-negotiable step regardless of how much the AI had already explained.

prompt: Asked for a pull request title and description for the branch containing these changes.
ai_output: Drafted a title and a structured description separating the code fix from the documentation changes, including a section specifically flagging the one unresolved design question (embedded vs. standalone defects) so a reviewing teammate would see it without needing to read the full diff themselves.
notes: Used as-is for the actual PR.
